items.old: class MyTable extends TableComponent (or any DS component you subclass)
items.note: TableComponent gained one member: `cellLink`. Subclassing a DS component is unsupported, but consumers do it, and a subclass declaring the same name now fails to build - TS4114 ("must have an 'override' modifier"), or TS2415 if the signature differs. `protected` is no protection: a redeclared protected member collides exactly as a public one does. ACTION only if you extend TableComponent and already declare `cellLink`: rename yours, or add `override` if you meant to replace ours.
items.verify: Build your app: no TS4114 or TS2415 is raised against a class that extends a DS component.

informational: `--ds-field-message-icon-offset` and `--ds-time-picker-focus-shadow` are public, overridable, and listed in the token reference - the supported way to retune either. Nothing changed in the components - if you hand-rolled around either because it looked unsupported, the override works and the workaround can go. They belong with the twelve named under 0.10.3.

If you applied 0.10.2 before its manifest was completed, two of its notes were reachable only from the CHANGELOG. First: components.md, the digest dist/ds carries for your own agent, had named --primary, --text-on-primary and --secondary as the active ds-sidenav-item defaults - the wash replaced them, so an override written against those three does not do what it looks like.

Second: `data-focus="inset"` (shipped in 0.10.2) draws the focus ring INSIDE the border box, for a subtree under an overflow:hidden ancestor that would otherwise clip it away entirely. It is the only focus style not pinned to :root - set it on the clipping element.

ds-table columns take a new optional `link: (row) => string | readonly unknown[] | null`. Nothing changes on a column that does not set it; see the class-surface entry if you SUBCLASS TableComponent. Where you compensated for an invisible row click by repeating the destination as a 'View Details' item in the row overflow menu, that item can go: give the name column `link` instead and the destination becomes a real <a> - tabbable as a link, Ctrl/Cmd-clickable, and announced as a link rather than as a table row. If you also set `rowInteractive`, note the pair costs two tab stops per row; the link alone is usually the better trade on a long list.

ds-card gains --ds-card-overflow, default visible. Opt-in on purpose: clipping a card also cuts the focus ring off any child at its edge, so where a clipped card holds focusable content pair it with data-focus="inset".
ds-button gains --ds-button-shadow and --ds-button-shadow-hover, both default none. Purely additive; -shadow-hover falls back to -shadow, and the focus/pressed hooks still win in their own states.

deleteList.why: A ::ng-deep reach into ds-card's inner .card to clip a full-bleed child (an image or footer strip) inside the card radius, because no token exposed it.
deleteList.replaceWith: --ds-card-overflow: clip on the card (clip, not hidden — it keeps the card from becoming a scroll container)

deleteList.why: A "View Details" entry in a row overflow menu that only repeats where the row already leads. It existed because the row click was the sole, invisible way in; a naming column with `link` makes the destination a real anchor, so the menu entry is a second control for the same navigation.
deleteList.replaceWith: set `link` on the column that names the record, and delete the menu item

deleteList.why: A deep selector into ds-button's inner <button> kept alive only by a resting box-shadow — background, colour, weight and border already had tokens.
